name: Nußdorf-Debant
kurzbeschreibung: Second-largest municipality in Osttirol, nestled at the foot of the Debanttaler Mountains, featuring a lakeside resort.
text:
Overview

Nußdorf-Debant is situated in the sun-drenched Lienz basin within the East Tyrolean district of Lienz, directly adjoining the district capital of Lienz to the east at an average valley altitude of 652 meters. With around 3,430 residents, this bustling market town is the third-largest municipality in East Tyrol. Covering an expansive territory of 53.4 square kilometers, the community comprises the historic hillside village of Nußdorf on the foot of the Nußdorfer Berg alongside the modern residential and commercial district of Debant along the Drau river plains. The geographic setting offers a striking contrast: while the valley floor features modern commerce, approximately 67 percent of the municipal land lies protected within the High Tauern National Park. To the north rise the towering three-thousand-meter peaks of the Schober Group, including the Hochschober and Glödis, while to the south opens the rugged panorama of the Lienz Dolomites.

History

Human habitation in the area traces back to the Neolithic and Iron Ages, verified by ancient discoveries at Breitegg. In Roman antiquity, the territory bordered directly on Municipium Claudium Aguntum, the only Roman city in ancient Tyrol, whose main archaeological site lies in neighboring Dölsach; the municipality's official coat of arms displays the celebrated bronze 'Girl of Aguntum'. The church in Nußdorf was first documented in 1274. An architectural treasure is the late Gothic branch church of St. Helena in Nußdorf, consecrated around 1500, preserving vibrant period frescoes and a Baroque high altar. In Debant, renowned Austrian architect Clemens Holzmeister designed the striking modern parish church of the Holy Spirit between 1970 and 1972. In 1939, Obernußdorf and Unternußdorf merged into a single municipality, officially elevated to market town status in 1995.

Getting There

Nußdorf-Debant enjoys exceptional transport links due to its direct proximity to Lienz. By car, drivers follow the B100 Drautalstraße eastward from Lienz in just three minutes, or travel from Carinthia via Spittal an der Drau. Coming from the north (Salzburg/Munich), motorists pass through the Felbertauern Tunnel on the B108 to Lienz and continue onto the B100. Rail passengers arrive at Lienz Hauptbahnhof along the Drau Valley Railway, served frequently by regional and intercity services. From Lienz station, frequent regional VVT buses connect to Nußdorf and Debant in merely five to eight minutes. Furthermore, cyclists can easily reach the town via the paved international Drau Cycle Path (R1).

Tips

An extraordinary natural gem is the 16-kilometer-long Debanttal, celebrated as the longest continuous alpine pasture valley in Austria, cutting deep into the high-alpine sanctuary of the High Tauern National Park. From the Seichenbrunn car park, the Debanttal Nature and Culture Trail winds along the rushing mountain torrent past the historic Hofalm pasture—featuring an alpine museum and show dairy—up to the Lienzer Hütte at 1,977 meters. Experienced trekkers can push onward to the turquoise waters of the Wangenitzsee at 2,465 meters and the Wangenitzseehütte. History enthusiasts should explore the adjacent Aguntum Archaeological Park with its 18-meter observation tower and Roman baths, while leisure cyclists appreciate the scenic Drau river trail.
